archetypes.name: sort-invariant
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces stamp-presence-first ordering with seeded $ACTUAL_VERSION and an explicit off-by-one failure mode (#4); the algorithm's seeding-then-fill invariant is load-bearing for the entire prune redesign.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan builds the retained set by seeding $ACTUAL_VERSION first, then filling to KEEP_VERSIONS=8 — Failure Mode #4 warns of an off-by-one (9 dirs) if seeding happens after selection. Verify the seeding algorithm resolves unambiguously in three cases: (a) $ACTUAL_VERSION ranks naturally as #8, (b) $ACTUAL_VERSION ranks outside the top-8, and (c) $ACTUAL_VERSION is the only stamped entry among many un-stamped dirs — in each case the plan must produce exactly 8 retained dirs, not 9. Confirm the already-latest code path in upgrade-larch.sh explicitly binds ACTUAL_VERSION from CURRENT_INSTALLED_VERSION before calling the shared prune helper, as required by Approach step 2 and Failure Mode #5 — trace the existing already-latest branch to locate where this assignment must be inserted. Verify that the stamp-presence-first, timestamp-descending, version-string-tiebreak sort can be implemented under Bash 3.2 constraints (no declare -A, no mapfile, no sort -k on shell arrays) and that the approach follows the same tab-separated output pattern already used by list_cached_versions_by_mtime, which pipes to sort -k1,1n -k2,2. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: depth-claim
archetypes.rationale: The plan's -maxdepth 5 bound for /cleanup newest-activity scan is a hard quantitative claim whose correctness determines whether active implement sessions are misclassified stale; the test must exercise the exact depth-5 path, not a shallower proxy.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan justifies -maxdepth 5 by asserting that larch-logs/implement/RUN_ID/round-1/findings.md is depth-5 from the session root — verify this depth count against files actually written to $IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR during an implement run, using evidence from skills/review-and-fix/scripts/test-review-and-fix.sh and the larch-logs/implement path constructions visible there. The new test-cleanup.sh must create the fresh artifact at the full path larch-logs/implement/RUN_ID/round-1/findings.md (depth-5) to exercise the boundary — not at a shallower stand-in such as larch-logs/round-1/findings.md (depth-3); check whether the plan's test specification is precise enough to require the correct depth rather than any five-level path. Confirm there is no actively-written session tmpdir artifact at depth greater than 5 for design or review sessions, particularly check whether design plan-review artifacts (committed at larch-logs/design/RUN_ID/plan-review/round-N/findings-classification.tsv, depth-6 in the repo) are also written at depth-6 in $DESIGN_TMPDIR during execution or whether design session writes stay shallow. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: live-migration
archetypes.rationale: Old-format .larch-keepalive files (7+ fields) remain on disk from in-flight sessions while new code writes the slim 2-field format; all reader code and test fixtures must be verified against both formats for hook routing continuity.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan changes the .larch-keepalive writer in session-setup.sh to emit only CLONE_PATH and SESSION_ID, but marks lib-resolve-implement-tmpdir.sh as comment-only — verify that its awk-based field parsers ($1=="CLONE_PATH" and $1=="SESSION_ID") tolerate extra fields so old-format files from sessions started before the upgrade do not break hook routing for /implement. Check that every fixture site writing .larch-keepalive content — including heredoc and printf constructions in test-keepalive-sentinel.sh, test-sessionstart-health.sh, and test-implement-bootstrap.sh — is updated to the slim two-field shape in the plan, because any fixture that still writes the old multi-field format may exercise the reader against the wrong payload and pass while masking a real regression. Verify there are no other scripts in skills/ or scripts/ that write .larch-keepalive directly (grep for .larch-keepalive write sites beyond session-setup.sh) that would produce the old format after the PR lands. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
